subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: Should Codex-backed WebChat sends preflight or repair native-thread liveness before returning `started`, or may they keep the current async ACK contract with stronger post-ACK recovery and health surfacing?
rationale: Both paths are plausible product contracts, but the current issue is specifically about user-visible trust in `chat.send started`; automation should not choose between fail-fast, forced rotation, delayed ACK semantics, and health/audit recovery without maintainer intent.

options.title: Preflight or fail before ACK
options.body: Require Codex-backed sends to prove native-thread admission enough to reach `turn/start`, force-rotate safely, or return a visible error before reporting `started`.

options.title: Keep async ACK with recovery
options.body: Preserve immediate `started` semantics but add durable monitoring, transcript/error persistence, and health/audit recovery for accepted sends that never reach a run.

options.title: Defer pending live fixture
options.body: Keep the issue open until a current-main fixture or live replay of the oversized native-thread state shows which contract is necessary.

recommendation.title: Preflight or fail before ACK
recommendation.body: Require Codex-backed sends to prove native-thread admission enough to reach `turn/start`, force-rotate safely, or return a visible error before reporting `started`.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently owned the merged native overflow rotation path most directly tied to the unresolved Codex thread-liveness behavior.
